COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
WPMS No. 822 of 2022
Shri S.K.Mishra, ACJ.
Shri R.C.Khulbe, J. 
 Mr. U. K. Uniyal, learned Senior 
Counsel, assisted by Mr. Vipul Sharma, 
learned counsel for the writ applicant.
Mr. K. N. Johsi, learned Deputy 
Advocate General for the State of 
Uttarakhand/respondent no.1. 
Mr. Suyash Pant, learned counsel 
for the respondent no.2. 
Mr. Rakesh Thapaliyal, learned 
Assistant Solicitor General, learned
counsel for the Union of India/
respondent no.3. 
Issue notice to the respondent no.4. 
Requisites for issuance of notice on 
the opposite party no. 4 through 
registered post/speed post, 
acknowledgement due, be filed within 
ten days. Notice be made returnable 
within six weeks. 
In the interregnum, we pass the 
following order 
(i) Respondent no. 2 will carry on 
the counseling for admission to
the undergraduate courses in the 
homeopathy stream qua those 
candidates who have qualified 
the NEET along with other 
candidates under the prevailing 
regime. 
(ii) In case any surplus seats are 
left, the concerned institutions 
will be permitted to provisionally  admit students in the 
Homeopathy stream qua 
undergraduate courses vis-a-vis
academic year 2021-2022
(iii) It is made clear that in case 
admission is granted to the 
petitioner, by the concerned 
institutions, by adopting the 
route as delineated in clause (ii) 
above–their admission being 
provisional, they would not be 
allowed to claim any equities in 
case they fail in the writ petition. 
We have passed this order keeping 
in view the observations made by the 
Hon’ble High Court of Karnatka in Writ 
Petition No. 100650 of 2021 on 
31.08.2021 and the Hon’ble High Court 
of Delhi in the case of Priyanshu 
Undaviya and others vs. Union of India 
and others, in WP(C) 451 of 2022 on 
25.02.2022. 
List this matter on 17th June, 2022. 
 (R.C.Khulbe, J.) (S.K.Mishra, ACJ.)
22.04.2022 Kaushal
